text:
margo: deploy-bot just pinged me  eu-dedicated canary p95 and a tiny 5xx uptick during the change window.

deploy-bot: alert: canary.p95=740ms (+230ms vs baseline) over 6m; 5xx_rate +1.7%. Suggested: PAUSE rollout and run focused probes. auto-rollback=false (change-window tag).

devon: What landed? I see the vectorized-matmul flag flip and a tiny allocator change in this batch.

lee: yes  vectorized-matmul toggle + allocator tuning. Local benches looked fine but we skipped multi-AZ soak.

ops_oncall: Since auto-rollback is suppressed, we need a manual mitigation plan. Proposing a conservative traffic split (60/40 back to prior stable) and pin the canary for debugging.

margo: agree. Also loop CS for affected early-access customers and legal for wording.

deploy-bot: helpful commands:
- traffic split 60/40: `redwood traffic set --pool eu-dedicated --route default --split 60:40 --to v2.3.14,v2.6.0`
- pin canary: `redwood pin --instance canary-eu --version v2.6.0`
- full rollback: `redwood rollback --pool eu-dedicated --to v2.3.14`

devon: I'll apply the split and tail the `gpu_sync_delay` and `alloc_fail` logs filtered by version.

lee: I'll open a revert PR that undoes the vectorized-matmul toggle and add a short perf/soak job to run against canary once CI passes.

cs_lead: I'll draft a short customer note for the EA list: 1-2 lines, link to monitor, ops contact. Legal please quick-review.

legal: quick ack. Keep language factual: no data loss expected, mitigation in progress. Avoid commitments on SLA changes.

devon: applying now.

deploy-bot: action started (requested by devon). rollout id: r-685432-01

devon: applied. monitor: https://telemetry.redwood/prod/eu-dedicated/r-685432-01

margo: +8m update? any signals on which variant is showing the tail?

devon: live numbers:
```
overall_p95: 520ms
v2.3.14_p95: 500ms
v2.6.0_p95: 740ms
5xx_overall: 0.8%
5xx_v2.6.0: 1.9%
```

lee: that isolates it to v2.6.0 (the new flag path). Revert PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/release/pull/4599 (cherry-pick + revert toggle). CI queued.

margo: Good. Checklist for this thread:
- [x] manual traffic split applied
- [x] canary pinned
- [x] EA customers notified by CS
- [ ] revert PR merged + canary redeploy
- [ ] update release notes explaining temporary toggle disablement
- [ ] post-mortem if unresolved after 2h

deploy-bot: note: canary redeploy will be gated on CI + prometheus health checks. auto-rollback remains suppressed for this change window.

devon: tailing logs now. errors like `gpu_sync_delay` are concentrated on hosts running v2.6.0.

cs_lead: Sent EA note: "We observed increased tail latency during canary; we've partially routed traffic to prior stable while engineering investigates. No data loss expected. Live monitor: https://telemetry.redwood/prod/eu-dedicated/r-685432-01. Ops contact: ops_oncall." Legal cleared.

lee: PR green and merged. Scheduling canary-only redeploy with the revert.

deploy-bot: canary redeploy triggered by lee. rollout id: r-685432-02. Health checks will gate promotion.

margo: monitoring. please post a +5m, +15m, +30m update.

devon: +5m: overall p95 ~495ms, v2.6.0 (revert) p95 ~510ms, 5xxs normalized. +15m: overall p95 485ms; looks stable so far.

margo: If revert holds for 30m soak, we'll re-roll remaining traffic and update release notes. Lee please add explanation in the PR about why the toggle was reverted and steps for future validation.

lee: will add release note snippet and a perf-soak checklist in the PR.

ops_oncall: maintaining watch. If anyone wants a full rollback instead of re-roll, add a thumbs-up reaction from an ops lead and ping legal for comms changes.

margo: good runbook execution, thanks team. I'll keep thread open for 2h then close if stable. :thumbsup:
